 BURNET, CONCHO, CORYELL,                                 §
 LAMPASSAS, LLANO, MASON,                                 §         ADMINISTRATIVE
 MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS,                         §           HEARINGS
 SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN,                         §
 AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                                  §

   ALBERT L. ANDERSON FAMILY LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AND DEANN
     DUNGAN'S OBJECTIONS TO APPLICANTS' DIRECT TESTIMONY

         Albert L. Anderson Family Limited Partnership ("Anderson Partnership") and DeAnn

Dungan (collectively, "Intervenors"), pursuant to 16 Texas Administrative Code ("TAC") § 22.71

and the procedural orders governing this proceeding, hereby file these objections to the direct

testimony of Applicants' witnesses filed in support of the Joint Application of Oncor Electric

Delivery Company LLC ("Oncor") and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation ("LCRA TSC")

(collectively, "Applicants").

         Intervenors own and steward Apache Crossing Ranch-approximately 620 acres in

Menard County, Texas-which lies directly in the path of Link M8. The Applicants' own

Environmental Assessment ("EA") demonstrates that M8 is among the most impactful link

segments in the entire 15-county study area. These objections identify the specific deficiencies in

Applicants' testimony that, if credited, would lead to the approval of a route that the evidence does

not support.




4922-5482-8973
           I. OBJECTIONS TO THE TESTIMONY OF RUSSELL J. MARUSAK

   A. Marusak's Blanket Prudent Avoidance Compliance Assertion Is Unsupported as to
      Link M8
       Marusak testifies that all alternative routes "adhere to the Commission' s policy of prudent

avoidance." (Marusak Direct at 21:11-12)

       Objection. Prudent avoidance under 16 TAC § 25.101(a)(6) requires "the limiting of

exposures to electric and magnetic fields that can be avoided with reasonable investments of

money and effort." Link M8 places a 765-kV transmission line-the highest voltage class used in

the United States-within 95 feet of a single-family residence. The EMF exposure at that distance

from a 765-kV line is substantially greater than it would be at the distances maintained by

alternative links in the same corridor; M32 and M33 each have only 1 habitable structure within

500 feet. Marusak's testimony provides no analysis of the EMF exposure levels at the habitable

structures along M8, no comparison of those levels to the exposure that would result from

alternative links, and no explanation of why placing a 765-kV line 95 feet from a residence

constitutes "limiting" EMF exposure "that can be avoided with reasonable investments of money

and effort." The Commission should disregard this conclusory assertion as applied to Link M8.


   B. Link M8's Habitable Structure Count Defeats the Community Values Analysis
       Marusak testifies that the routing process "identif[ied] areas where constraints are absent

or fewer." (Marusak Direct at 9:22-10:2)


       Objection. This assertion is unsupported as applied to Link M8 under the community

values criterion of PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A). The Applicants' own data shows M8 has 13 habitable

structures within 500 feet of its centerline-the highest count of any link in the Menard County

corridor--while the links it replaced (M32 and M33) have 1 structure each. A routing process that

produces a link with 1,200% more habitable structure exposure than the segments it replaced has



                                                2
 not identified an area where "constraints are absent or fewer." To the contrary, M8 was routed into

a more constrained area, not away from one. The Commission should evaluate this testimony

against the Applicants' own habitable structure data.


   C. The Post-Meeting Addition of Link M8 Undermines the Public Involvement Process
       Marusak testifies that, following the public meetings, Halff and Kimley-Horn "considered

modifications to preliminary alternative route links, removal of preliminary route links, and the

addition of new alternative route links." (Marusak Direct at 17: 18-22)He further testifies that the

public involvement program satisfied the requirements of 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4).


       Objection. The purpose of the public meeting requirement under 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4) is

to provide affected landowners the opportunity to comment on proposed routes befbre the

Application is filed. Link M8 was not presented at any of the three public meetings held in June

2025. The landowners along the Highway 29 corridor near Hext, Texas-the community most

directly impacted by M8-had no opportunity to provide input on this link during the formal public

involvement process. While the rule permits post-meeting modifications, adding a fundamentally

new link through a populated residential corridor qfter the meetings, without any supplemental

notice or opportunity for comment, defeats the purpose of the statutory public participation

requirement. Marusak' s testimony that the public involvement process was adequate is misleading

as applied to the landowners affected by Link M8.


   D. Marusak's Conclusion That Construction Would Not Have "Significant Impact" on
      Cultural Resources Is Unsupported as to M8
       Marusak testifies that "[clonstruction of the Proposed Transmission Line Project should

not have a significant impact on existing... cultural resources." (Marusak Direct at 21:21-22:2)


       Objection. This blanket conclusion is directly contradicted by the EA' s own data. Table

7-9 (Appendix F) identifies the Pegleg Crossing on the San Saba Official Texas Historical Marker


                                                 3
 at just 110 feet from the M8 centerline-one of only five such markers within 1,000 feet of any

link across the entire 15-county study area. A 765-kV line with approximately 200-foot steel lattice

towers at 110 feet from a state historical marker would destroy the historical character and setting

the marker commemorates. Marusak's testimony offers no site-specific analysis of M8' s impact

on the Pegleg Crossing marker, the adjacent Darley Infant Cemetery (565 feet), or the Indian

artifacts documented along the San Saba River on Intervenor' s Property. The Commission should

reject this conclusory statement as applied to Link M8. See PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(C) (requiring

the Commission to consider "historical and aesthetic values").


           II. OBJECTIONS TO THE TESTIMONY OF CASEY D. PETTY, P.E.

   A. Petty's Testimony Fails to Provide Link-Level Analysis of M8
       Petty testifies that all 122 filed routes comply with the Commission's policy of prudent

avoidance. (Petty Direct at 16:3-4)


        Objection. To the extent any filed route includes Link M8, Petty's assertion of statutory

compliance is unsupported. Petty's routing memorandum (Exhibit CDP-6) provides no specific

analysis of why routes incorporating M8-with its 13 habitable structures, 7.5 miles of highway

paralleling, 4.8 miles of riparian crossings, 18 stream crossings, an Official Texas Historical

Marker at 110 feet, and a cemetery at 565 feet-satisfy the statutory routing criteria. The testimony

treats all 122 routes as interchangeably compliant, which obscures the material differences

between individual links. The Commission's evaluation under PURA § 37.056(c)(4) requires link-

level analysis, and Petty' s route-level generalizations are insufficient.




                                                   4
          III. OBJECTIONS TO THE TESTIMONY OF CORIN E. COOLEY, P.E.

   A. Cooley's Testimony on Engineering Constraints Omits the Demonstrated Flood
      Risk in the M8 Corridor
       Cooley testifies that "the study area does not contain any known engineering constraints

that cannot be resolved with additional consideration during the design and construction phases"

and acknowledges that      "the Applicants have not performed on-the-ground geotechnical or

subsurface surveys on private properties." (Cooley Direct at 20:14-21)

       Objection. This testimony is materially incomplete as applied to Link M8. Menard County

experienced record flooding in July 2025 (FEMA-4879-DR-TX), with the San Saba River near

Brady reaching a record crest of 30.53 feet. FEMA has not completed modern flood hazard

mapping for Menard County-only 1987-1991 maps exist. Cooley's testimony does not address

how the Applicants propose to ensure the structural integrity and reliability of 765-kV steel lattice

towers in a watershed with demonstrated catastrophic flood risk and no modern flood data. The

absence of any flood risk analysis for the M8 corridor is a material omission.


   B. The Cost Estimates Lack Per-Link Granularity
       Cooley testifies that estimated transmission line costs range from approximately $1.636

billion to $1.858 billion depending on the route selected. (Cooley Direct at 16:9-12)


       Objection. Cooley's testimony provides cost estimates at the route level but not per-link

cost breakdowns. Without link-level cost data, the Commission cannot assess the incremental cost

of Link M8 as compared to alternative links in the same corridor (e.g., M32, M33, V-series, K-

series). The Commission's analysis under PURA § 37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B)

requires consideration of costs as a routing factor. To the extent Cooley's testimony is offered to

support the cost-reasonableness of routes incorporating Link M8, it is incomplete without per-link

data sufficient for comparison.



                                                  5
               IV. OBJECTIONS TO THE TESTIMONY OF KELLY WELLS

   A. The Post-Meeting Addition of Link M8 Denies Parties of Public Participation

       Wells testifies that "LCRA TSC and Oncor have followed applicable regulatory

requirements, including notice requirements." (Wells Direct at 16:6-10)


       Objection. To the extent Wells' testimony certifies the public participation process as

adequate for Link M8, Intervenors object on the same grounds stated in Section I. C. The affected

landowners along the Highway 29 corridor near Hext received no notice of Link M8 before the

public meetings because M8 did not exist at that time. Wells' blanket certification does not address

the specific deficiency created by the post-meeting addition of a high-impact link through a

community that had no opportunity to comment on it.

   B. Wells' Testimony Fails to Provide Link-Level Analysis

       Wells testifies that LCRA TSC "supports all 122 routes in the Application, and any

reasonably forward-progressing route that can be delineated from the 171 individual route

segments as viable options." (Wells Direct at 15: 16-18)


       Objection. This undifferentiated endorsement of all 171 link segments, without any link-

level evaluation, should be given no weight in the Commission's route-selection analysis. The

Commission's task is to evaluate and compare links, not to ratify a blanket endorsement.

   C. Wells' Testimony Does Not Address the Commission's Hierarchical Routing
      Preferences

       Wells testifies that the filed routes "utilize compatible routing corridors by paralleling

existing ROW, property lines, and other natural or cultural features." (Wells Direct at 14:18-20)


       Objection. Link M8 parallels approximately 7.5 miles of State Highway 29 ROW but only

approximately 0.8 miles of existing transmission line ROW. The Commission's routing criteria at

16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B) list four routing factors in a specific order: subsection (i) addresses


                                                 6
 paralleling existing compatible rights - of-way for electric facilities ·, subsection ( ii ) addresses

paralleling roads, highways, and railroads. Petty's testimony does not explain why Link M8's

heavy reliance on highway paralleling, rather than paralleling existing electric facilities, is

consistent with the structure of the Commission' s rule. This omission is material because the rule

was designed to minimize new visual and land-use impacts by keeping transmission infrastructure

near existing transmission corridors wherever feasible.


                V. OBJECTION TO THE TESTIMONY OF JARED GURLEY

          Gurley sponsors the need case for the Proposed Transmission Line Project, including the

Permian Basin Reliability Plan and the Commission' s orders directing construction of Import Path

2.

          Objection. Intervenors offer no opinion on whether a transmission need exists for Import

Path 2. However, to the extent Gurley's testimony is offered or cited to justify the selection ofLink

M8 over alternative links in the Menard County corridor, Intervenors obj ect. The reliability need

identified in the Permian Basin Reliability Plan is for a 765-kV transmission line between Bell

County East and Big Hill-it does not specify the route or prescribe Link M8. The need for the

project does not excuse the selection of a specific link that fails to satisfy the routing criteria of

PURA § 37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B). To the extent Applicants argue that

reliability urgency or the December 2030 energization date justifies less scrutiny of individual link

impacts, Intervenors obj ect and reserve the right to challenge that argument at the hearing on the

merits.




                                                  7
                                   VI. GENERAL OBJECTIONS

   A. Lack of Specific Route Inquiry. Intervenors obj ect to any testimony or exhibit that

assumes or implies that all 171 link segments in the Application are equally compliant with PURA

§ 37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC § 25.101. The statutory and regulatory framework requires the

Commission to evaluate the specific impacts of each link, and blanket compliance assertions

obscure material differences between links.

   B. Evidentiary Objections. Intervenors obj ect to any testimony or exhibit to the extent it is

offered without proper foundation, is speculative, constitutes an improper legal conclusion, or is

outside the scope of the witness' s expertise.

   C. Reservation of Rights. Intervenors reserve the right to supplement these obj ections and to

raise additional objections at the hearing on the merits based on further discovery, investigation,

or testimony.


                                           VII. PRAYER

       For the foregoing reasons, Intervenors respectfully request that the Administrative Law

Judge and the Commission:

    1. Sustain the objections set forth herein;
   2. Disregard or give no weight to the portions of Applicants' testimony identified above as
      they relate to Link M8;
   3. Require Applicants to provide link-level analysis and data sufficient for the Commission
      to conduct the evaluation required by PURA § 37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC § 25.101; and

   4. Grant Intervenors such other and further relief as the Commission deems just and
      appropriate.
